I'm hard of hearing. Sirens are generally loud enough for me to hear them, but the flashing lights help too. I can also see people flip me off when I can't hear their horn. (Just kidding. Mostly.) 

I think the ones you really have to watch out for are the people who text and drive and the people who drive home after drinking at the bar.

Also, I don't understand why people are giving you such nasty responses. I've been asked before if I have difficulty driving because I'm hard of hearing. It's a fair question and I don't think you were being insensitive for asking. There is more to listen for than just sirens. But for the most part, my hearing doesn't affect my ability to drive.
Yep!

A bike bell, the chiming of the railroad crossing bars, a truck honking to GTFO of their way, someone yelling, a nearby car crash, someone beeping, the parking attendant, the GPS trying its best to give me directions
I'm from the USA. We don't have any requirements like that where I live. I'd be totally fucked if I lived by you! In that case, I absolutely shouldn't be on the road without really good hearing aids.

Yeah, definitely things a good driver should notice with or without their hearing! But someone with full hearing could have an advantage because they have an extra level of awareness that I don't.
